abstract.p: Greetings SIGIR Community! We are very excited for SIGIR 2025 beginning in just a few weeks in Padova Italy (July 13-17), co-located with ICTIR (July 18) (serendipitously happening at the same time as the Iron Maiden Run for Your Lives World Tour (concert in Padova July 13)). The ACM, including SIGIR, remains committed to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) and this year we successfully petitioned the ACM to add caste as a protected group to the ACM's DEI statement. For more information about DEI and the ACM, please see https://www.acm.org/di versity-inclusion. If you are interested in promoting DEI at SIGIR, we are currently seeking volunteers to lead the SIGIR DEI initiatives. Please reach out to exec SIGIR@acm.org for more information. In the last three years we experimented with adding a few new volunteer roles (Community Relations Coordinator intended to serve as a contact point for folks wishing to organize social events at the conferences), and separated the roles of Information Director and IRList Moderator. We get an 'E' for Effort on that-it was a good thought. Moving forward we will merge the three roles to the Information Director role, to be shared by two volunteers. We are currently considering the role of the Student Affairs Chairs, as the conferences usually have their own Student Affairs Chairs, and it is not clear that the role is needed at the SIG level. The Exec Committee began two initiatives that will be picked up by the next Exec Committee. The first is a revamp of the of the sigir.org website to make it more functional, and to highlight current activities. The second is a re-examination of the reviewing process. We have taken feedback from the community, and talked to other organizations about their processes and efforts to improve the quality of reviews, and how they transitioned from an annual submission model, to rolling submission deadlines, revise and resubmit, open review, etc. The Gerard Salton Award Committee suggested to change the cadence of the award from every three years to every two, because the community is now large enough to support the additional awards. The Gerard Salton Award is SIGIR's highest honor. It recognizes those who have made significant, sustained and continuing contributions to research in information retrieval. The Salton Award honored Ellen Voorhees in 2024 for her contributions to the systematic evaluation of information retrieval systems at scale. The next award will be in 2026.
